\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Independent Bernoulli Boolean measure]
\lean{Randomized.iidBernoulli}
\statementsource{Vad12}{
  pdf-bf2ce5422088-p171-b002,
  pdf-bf2ce5422088-p289-b002
}
\statementsource{vershynin-hdp-book}{
  pdf-681b6f3d947f-p018-b002,
  pdf-681b6f3d947f-p025-b008
}
\statementsource{arora-barak-ch07-randomized-computation}{
  pdf-26d95080dbde-p008-b001,
  pdf-26d95080dbde-p008-b002
}
\label{Randomized.iidBernoulli}
\leanok
For a natural number $k$, a nonnegative real parameter $p\leq 1$, let the measure on
Boolean vectors of length $k$ be the product measure whose coordinate marginals are
Bernoulli distributions with success parameter $p$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Success count]
\lean{Randomized.successCount}
\statementsource{Vad12}{pdf-bf2ce5422088-p289-b002}
\statementsource{vershynin-hdp-book}{pdf-681b6f3d947f-p025-b008}
\label{Randomized.successCount}
\leanok
For a Boolean sequence $\omega$ of length $k$, its success count is the number of
coordinates at which $\omega$ is true, viewed as a real number.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Coordinate indicator]
\lean{Randomized.coordIndicator}
\statementsource{Vad12}{pdf-bf2ce5422088-p289-b002}
\statementsource{vershynin-hdp-book}{pdf-681b6f3d947f-p025-b008}
\label{Randomized.coordIndicator}
\leanok
For a Boolean sequence $\omega$ of length $k$ and a coordinate $i$, the indicator of
success at $i$ is $1$ if $\omega_i$ is true and $0$ otherwise, viewed as a real number.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Measurability of a coordinate indicator]
\lean{Randomized.measurable_coordIndicator}
\label{Randomized.measurable_coordIndicator}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.coordIndicator}
\difficulty{3}
For every natural number $k$ and coordinate $i\in\{0,\ldots,k-1\}$, the function on
Boolean vectors of length $k$ that equals $1$ when coordinate $i$ is true and $0$
otherwise is measurable.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Mean of a Bernoulli coordinate]
\lean{Randomized.integral_coordIndicator}
\label{Randomized.integral_coordIndicator}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.coordIndicator, Randomized.iidBernoulli}
\difficulty{4}
Let $p\in\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ satisfy $p\le 1$, let $k$ be a natural number, and let
$i<k$. Choose a Boolean vector of length $k$ with independent coordinates, each equal to
true with probability $p$. The expected value of the indicator that coordinate $i$ is
true is $p$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Integrability of a Bernoulli coordinate indicator]
\lean{Randomized.integrable_coordIndicator}
\label{Randomized.integrable_coordIndicator}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.coordIndicator, Randomized.iidBernoulli, Randomized.measurable_coordIndicator}
\difficulty{4}
Let $p\in[0,1]$, let $k$ be a natural number, and let $i$ be a coordinate in
$\{0,\ldots,k-1\}$. Under the product measure on $k$ independent Bernoulli-$p$ bits, the
indicator of whether coordinate $i$ equals true is integrable.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Independence of coordinate indicators]
\lean{Randomized.iIndepFun_coordIndicator}
\label{Randomized.iIndepFun_coordIndicator}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.coordIndicator, Randomized.iidBernoulli}
\difficulty{1}
Let $p$ be a nonnegative real number with $p\le 1$, and let $k$ be a natural number.
Under the product measure on Boolean strings of length $k$ whose coordinates are
independent Bernoulli variables with parameter $p$, the coordinate indicator random
variables are mutually independent.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Subgaussian bound for a centered Bernoulli coordinate]
\lean{Randomized.hasSubgaussianMGF_coordIndicator_sub}
\label{Randomized.hasSubgaussianMGF_coordIndicator_sub}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.coordIndicator, Randomized.iidBernoulli, Randomized.integrable_coordIndicator, Randomized.integral_coordIndicator, Randomized.measurable_coordIndicator}
\difficulty{5}
Let $p$ be a nonnegative real number with $p\leq 1$, let $k$ be a natural number, and
choose a coordinate $i$ among $k$ independent Boolean coordinates, each equal to true
with probability $p$. Under their product distribution, the coordinate indicator minus
$p$ has a subgaussian moment generating function with variance proxy $(1/2)^2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Subgaussian bound for a reversed centered Bernoulli coordinate]
\lean{Randomized.hasSubgaussianMGF_sub_coordIndicator}
\label{Randomized.hasSubgaussianMGF_sub_coordIndicator}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.coordIndicator, Randomized.hasSubgaussianMGF_coordIndicator_sub, Randomized.iidBernoulli}
\difficulty{3}
Let $p$ be a nonnegative real number with $p\leq 1$, let $k$ be a natural number, and
choose a coordinate $i$ among $k$ independent Boolean coordinates, each equal to true
with probability $p$. Under their product distribution, $p$ minus the coordinate
indicator has a subgaussian moment generating function with variance proxy $(1/2)^2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Bernoulli sum tail bound]
\lean{Randomized.iidBernoulli_tail_le}
\label{Randomized.iidBernoulli_tail_le}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.iidBernoulli}
\difficulty{3}
Let $p$ be a nonnegative real number with $p\le 1$, and let $k>0$. On the product
distribution of $k$ independent Bernoulli-$p$ bits, suppose $Y_1,\ldots,Y_k$ are
independent random variables, each with sub-Gaussian moment-generating-function
parameter $(1/2)^2$. For every $t\ge 0$, the probability that $\sum_{i=1}^k Y_i\ge tk$
is at most $\exp(-2t^2k)$.
\end{theorem}

Let $p\in[0,1]$, let $\varepsilon>0$ satisfy $\tfrac12+\varepsilon\le p$, and let $k$ be
a positive integer. For $k$ independent Bernoulli trials with success probability $p$,
the probability that at most half of the trials succeed is at most
$\exp(-2\varepsilon^2k)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Bernoulli average concentration]
\lean{Randomized.iid_bernoulli_avg_concentration_of_le}
\label{Randomized.iid_bernoulli_avg_concentration_of_le}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.iidBernoulli, Randomized.iid_bernoulli_avg_concentration, Randomized.successCount}
\difficulty{4}
Let $p\in[0,1]$, let $\varepsilon>0$, and let $0<\delta\le 1$. If $k$ is a natural
number satisfying $\log(2/\delta)/(2\varepsilon^2)\le k$, then under the product
distribution of $k$ independent Bernoulli-$p$ bits, the probability that the absolute
difference between the fraction of successes and $p$ exceeds $\varepsilon$ is at most
$\delta$.
\end{theorem}
